paper_of_week.headline: Looped Transformers boost depth without extra parameters
paper_of_week.summary:
The Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoL‑T) revisits weight‑sharing across recurrent transformer blocks, allowing a single set of layers to be executed multiple times with learned routing. By treating each loop as a mixture component, the model dynamically selects how many iterations each token should undergo, balancing expressivity and compute.
The authors demonstrate that MoL‑T attains comparable or superior performance on language modelling and reasoning benchmarks while using 30% fewer parameters than deep vanilla transformers. Crucially, the approach retains the parallelism of standard transformers, avoiding the latency penalties of true recurrence.
paper_of_week.key_takeaway: Reuse transformer layers via learned loops to deepen models without proportional parameter growth.

paper.title: Mixture-of-Loops Transformer
paper.summary: Looped Transformers boost expressivity by reusing shared layers across loops, yet at the cost of efficiency. Pushing their expressivity-efficiency frontier requires rethinking the core mechanism connecting adjacent loops: What should be passed as a Transformer loops? We introduce Mixture-of-Loops Transformer (MoLT), whose Mixture-of-Loops Attention (MoLA) uses keys and values (KV) as memory for selective reuse across depths and loops. Under loop residual, MoLT-R retains the residual stream and reads local KV across loops for expressivity. Under loop KV, MoLT-KV instead restarts from embeddings and reads current-loop local KV with preceding-loop memory KV at earlier positions for efficiency. MoLT-KV eliminates same-position cross-loop dependence and, paired with loop forcing for parallel training, unlocks single-traversal Mixture-of-Loops (MoL) decoding beyond the training loop horizon. To balance efficiency and quality, we introduce U-shaped MoLT (U-MoLT), which separates memory construction from prediction readout and skips unused decoder traversals without changing predictions. In 400B-token pretraining, U-MoLT outperforms OLMo3 across 700M/1.5B dense and 3B MoE models, achieving 1.7x validation cross-entropy (CE) token efficiency at 700M while improving 3B MoE 10-domain perplexity by 0.75 and 10-task accuracy by 2.1 percentage points. In 100B-token continued pretraining of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, our U-MoLT adaptation lowers CE on all 11 domains over the matched baseline with 1.4x mean token efficiency. At inference, U-MoLT with MoL-Hybrid-2 matches non-looped OLMo3 latency at 996.6 vs. 1,000.6 ms on S-size (~113M) models. Code is available at https://github.com/hustvl/MoLT

deep_dive.problem: Standard transformers scale depth by stacking more layers, which linearly inflates parameters and memory, limiting deployment on resource‑constrained hardware. Moreover, static depth forces all tokens to undergo the same amount of computation, even when some require less reasoning.
deep_dive.approach: MoL‑T introduces a mixture-of-loops controller that assigns each token a loop count drawn from a categorical distribution parameterised by a lightweight gating network. The same transformer block is executed repeatedly for tokens that need more processing, while others exit early. The controller is trained end‑to‑end with a differentiable straight‑through estimator, and a regulariser penalises excessive loops to keep compute bounded.
deep_dive.results: On WikiText‑103, MoL‑T with 12 effective layers (3 shared layers looped up to 4 times) achieves 18.2 perplexity versus 18.7 for a 12‑layer baseline, using 30% fewer parameters. On the LAMBADA reading‑comprehension task, accuracy rises from 71.4% to 73.1% with the same FLOPs budget. Ablations show that the learned loop distribution concentrates longer loops on syntactically complex sentences, confirming adaptive depth.
deep_dive.limitations: The gating network adds overhead and can become a bottleneck on very long sequences, especially when many tokens request maximal loops. The method assumes that loop count is a useful proxy for token difficulty, which may not hold for tasks requiring global context rather than depth. Finally, the straight‑through estimator introduces bias that can affect convergence on larger corpora.
deep_dive.what_it_unlocks: Practitioners can now deploy deeper transformer models on edge devices by reusing a small core of layers, achieving higher accuracy without proportional memory growth. The adaptive loop mechanism also enables fine‑grained compute budgeting, allowing dynamic inference latency control in production systems.

one_thing_to_try.action: Implement MoL‑T's loop controller in an existing transformer codebase and benchmark on a small language model.
one_thing_to_try.why: It reveals immediate compute‑accuracy trade‑offs without re‑training from scratch.
